evidence.title: Electric vehicle fleet transition program

initiatives.name: Ambition Zero Carbon Strategy
initiatives.summary: AstraZeneca is implementing enterprise-wide action to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 98% from global operations by 2026, with plans to be carbon negative by 2030. The company has allocated $1 billion from 2020 to achieve these targets and increased nature-based solutions investment to $400 million through AZ Forest.
initiatives.investmentSummary: $1 billion for emissions reduction, $400 million for AZ Forest

evidence.title: 200 million trees commitment expansion
evidence.summary: AstraZeneca expanded its AZ Forest programme commitment from 50 million to 200 million trees to be planted and maintained across six continents by 2030. This represents a significant increase in the company's nature-based climate solutions investment.
evidence.quote: Also in 2023, we strengthened our investment in nature-based solutions by expanding our AZ Forest programme to include planting and maintaining 200 million trees across six continents by 2030... Raised AZ Forest commitment to 200 million trees planted and stewarded by 2030 (from 50 million by 2025).

evidence.title: Ambition Zero Carbon strategy pursuing net zero by 2045
evidence.summary: AstraZeneca is pursuing ambitious science-based decarbonisation targets with 77.5% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions from 2015 baseline. The company aims to become carbon negative from 2030 for all residual GHG emissions and achieve net zero by 2045.
evidence.quote: In 2020, we launched our Ambition Zero Carbon strategy, through which we are pursuing ambitious science-based decarbonisation targets and making progress towards achieving net zero by 2045. We also aim to become carbon negative from 2030 for all residual GHG emissions.

evidence.title: Ambition Zero Carbon with $1 billion investment
evidence.summary: AstraZeneca is implementing enterprise-wide action to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 98% from global operations by 2026, with plans to be carbon negative by 2030. The company has allocated $1 billion from 2020 to achieve these targets and increased nature-based solutions investment to $400 million through AZ Forest.
evidence.quote: Taking into account climate-related risks and opportunities, we are taking enterprise-wide action to reduce GHG emissions from our global operations and fleet by 98% by 2026 (from a 2015 baseline) with a $1 billion spend budgeted from 2020... In 2023, we increased our investment in nature-based solutions to $400 million through AZ Forest, to mitigate our residual emissions and reach our net-zero SBTs to prepare for a low-carbon economy.

initiatives.name: Comprehensive Capital Expenditure Program

initiatives.name: AI and Data Science Implementation
initiatives.summary: AstraZeneca is implementing AI across research and development to transform disease biology understanding, accelerate drug discovery, and pioneer new clinical approaches. AI is also being deployed in operations to enhance manufacturing, supply chain automation, and quality standards.

evidence.title: AI transformation across R&D and operations
evidence.summary: AstraZeneca is implementing AI across research and development to transform disease biology understanding, accelerate drug discovery, and pioneer new clinical approaches. AI is also being deployed in operations to enhance manufacturing, supply chain automation, and quality standards.
evidence.quote: In research and development (R&D), AI transforms our understanding of disease biology; drives earlier diagnosis; and helps us create the next generation of medicines and pioneer new approaches in the clinic and beyond... In Operations, AI enhances manufacturing and supply, enabling us to respond more pro-actively, drive automation and robotics, and raise quality standards still further.

evidence.title: AI deployment across R&D and operations
evidence.summary: AstraZeneca is using AI and data science across 85% of small molecule programmes and implementing over 30 digital tools and AI solutions in operations. The company achieved significant productivity gains including 55% output increase and 44% lead time reduction at Wuxi plant.
evidence.quote: In R&D, we are now using AI and data science across 85% of our small molecule programmes – from target identification to clinical trials. By implementing over 30 digital tools and AI solutions, for selected processes and products, our plant in Wuxi, China, has achieved a 55% output increase, 44% lead time reduction and a 54% boost in productivity.

initiatives.name: Renewable Energy and Sustainability Partnerships
initiatives.summary: AstraZeneca signed a 10-year PPA with Statkraft for 200 GWh per year from new wind farms in Sweden, covering 80% of electricity needs at Gothenburg and Södertälje sites. Additional agreements include biomethane supply in China and 15-year agreement with Future Biogas.

evidence.title: Renewable energy power purchase agreements
evidence.summary: AstraZeneca signed a 10-year PPA with Statkraft for 200 GWh per year from new wind farms in Sweden, covering 80% of electricity needs at Gothenburg and Södertälje sites. Additional agreements include biomethane supply in China and 15-year agreement with Future Biogas.
evidence.quote: At the beginning of 2024, a 10-year PPA came into effect with Statkraft, Europe's largest renewable energy producer, to source electricity from three new wind farms in Sweden that will supply 200 gigawatt hours (GWh) per year from new-to-grid projects. This provides additional zero carbon electricity to the grid and is expected to correspond to approximately 80% of our total electricity needs at our Gothenburg and Södertälje sites.

evidence.title: Renewable natural gas collaboration with Vanguard Renewables
evidence.summary: AstraZeneca is collaborating with Vanguard Renewables to enable delivery of renewable natural gas to all US sites by end of 2026. The collaboration is expected to provide up to 230 GWh per year of RNG, equivalent to 46% of total global gas consumption.
evidence.quote: Since 2023, we have been collaborating with Vanguard Renewables to enable the delivery of renewable natural gas (RNG – biomethane) to all of our sites in the US by the end of 2026, launching at our Newark campus in Delaware. By 2026, this collaboration is expected to enable up to 230 GWh per year of RNG to be used across AstraZeneca's US sites, equivalent to 46% of our total global gas consumption.

initiatives.name: EU Taxonomy Compliance for Sustainable Activities
initiatives.summary: AstraZeneca has implemented the EU Taxonomy regulation classification system for sustainable economic activities, with 95% of revenue, 83% of capex, and 21% of opex being taxonomy-eligible under 'Manufacture of medicinal products'. However, the company assessed that their products do not meet substantial contribution criteria for alignment due to biodegradability requirements.

evidence.title: EU Taxonomy Compliance Implementation for Sustainable Activities
evidence.summary: AstraZeneca has implemented the EU Taxonomy regulation classification system for sustainable economic activities, with 95% of revenue, 83% of capex, and 21% of opex being taxonomy-eligible under 'Manufacture of medicinal products'. However, the company assessed that their products do not meet substantial contribution criteria for alignment due to biodegradability requirements.
evidence.quote: The Group has identified its Taxonomy-eligible activities by screening the economic activities in the Climate Delegated Act and the Environmental Delegated Act. The Group is eligible for a revenue-generating economic activity included in the Environmental Delegated Act for the environmental objective of Pollution Prevention and Control (PPC), namely, PPC 1.2 Manufacture of medicinal products.

initiatives.name: Ambitious Growth and Medicine Development

evidence.title: 15 new medicines target by 2030
evidence.summary: AstraZeneca has set a bold ambition to launch at least 15 new molecular entities between 2023 and 2030. This represents a major strategic commitment to innovation-led growth, with three new medicines already approved in 2023 as the first year of this eight-year goal.

AstraZeneca has one of the leading development pipelines in the sector and its strength in 2023 was evidenced by first approvals for three new medicines – the first year in our eight-year goal of launching at least 15 new molecular entities (NMEs) between 2023 and 2030.

evidence.title: Harmonised Listing Structure Implementation

This provides flexibility to access broader pool of capital and widens investor base, especially US institutional and retail investors.

On 2 February 2026, AstraZeneca Ordinary Shares were directly listed on the New York Stock Exchange, replacing the US listing of AstraZeneca ADSs on Nasdaq.

initiatives.name: Next-Generation Propellant Transition for Inhalers

evidence.title: Next-Generation Propellant Transition for Inhalers

initiatives.name: Respiratory Medicine Propellant Transition

evidence.title: Next-generation propellant transition for respiratory medicines

evidence.title: Cellectis gene-editing collaboration and investment

evidence.quote: A collaboration and proposed equity investment agreement with Cellectis, a clinical-stage biotechnology company, to leverage the Cellectis proprietary gene-editing technologies and manufacturing capabilities, to accelerate the development of next-generation therapeutics in areas of high unmet medical need. initiatives.name: Climate Risk Scenario Planning Framework
initiatives.summary: AstraZeneca has implemented comprehensive climate risk scenario analysis using three temperature pathways (+1.8°C, +2.7°C, +4.4°C) to assess physical and transition risks. The scenarios are used for deep-dive risk assessments of certain sites and data modeling for new project lifecycles through 2030 and 2050.

evidence.title: Climate Risk Scenario Planning Implementation
evidence.summary: AstraZeneca has implemented comprehensive climate risk scenario analysis using three temperature pathways (+1.8°C, +2.7°C, +4.4°C) to assess physical and transition risks. The scenarios are used for deep-dive risk assessments of certain sites and data modeling for new project lifecycles through 2030 and 2050.
evidence.quote: This scenario lays out a pathway and emissions trajectory that is aligned with the objectives of the Paris Agreement to limit global warming to well below 2°C, preferably to 1.5°C, by 2100, compared with pre-industrial levels. Metrics to quantify exposure to hazards in this scenario are used in deep-dive risk assessments for certain sites to pressure test how effective existing mitigations will be in 2030 and 2050.
